description: A SELECT from a stream returns the NET delta per logical row (Snowflake semantics), not the raw change log: a row inserted then updated inside the window is one INSERT of its FINAL image with METADATA$ISUPDATE false; inserted then deleted cancels out entirely; a PRE-EXISTING row updated (once or repeatedly) nets to one DELETE of the ORIGINAL image plus one INSERT of the FINAL image, both with METADATA$ISUPDATE true; and updated then deleted nets to a plain DELETE of the original image with ISUPDATE false. Offset semantics are pinned alongside - a plain SELECT does not consume while a DML read does, a ROLLBACK restores the offset, CREATE OR REPLACE resets it, and SHOW_INITIAL_ROWS seeds the existing rows as INSERTs after which consumption and accrual behave normally - as is APPEND_ONLY filtering, where only true inserts are recorded so a later delete does NOT remove the captured insert. SHOW STREAMS reports each stream's actual mode (it was once hardcoded to DEFAULT). Converted 1:1 from stream/StreamNetDeltaTest (now retired); the boolean METADATA$ISUPDATE is rendered with TO_VARCHAR and the SHOW STREAMS columns are read back through RESULT_SCAN, which is the SQL surface for what the Java read off the ResultSet by column index.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
CREATE STREAM st ON TABLE src
SELECT id || '|' || METADATA$ACTION || '|' || TO_VARCHAR(METADATA$ISUPDATE) AS r FROM st ORDER BY id
